summary: WebSocket-driven PTY and file/process control primitives expose full-host RCE on the installer
details: At agent startup (via `yeaft-agent` bin, `node index.js`, or the installed systemd/launchd/PM2 unit), the package opens a persistent WebSocket to a configured server and dispatches incoming messages through a router that grants the remote endpoint full control over the installer's host. `terminal_create` messages spawn a bash/PowerShell PTY (`pty.spawn(shell,...)`) in the agent's workDir, and `terminal_input` messages write attacker-supplied bytes directly into that PTY via `term.pty.write(msg.data)` — arbitrary shell command execution under whichever account runs the agent. The same router also handles `read_file` / `write_file` / `delete_files` / `move_files` / `upload_to_dir` (arbitrary filesystem read/write), `git_add` / `git_commit` / `git_push` (repo mutation and push under the installer's git identity), and `restart_agent` / `upgrade_agent` (writes 0o755 shell scripts, runs `npm install <pkg>@latest`, reloads systemd/launchd units, and re-execs the agent). On every start, `ensureYeaftSkills()` additionally `git clone`s or `git pull --ff-only`s https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git into `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev/` from an unpinned default branch, chmod 0o755s hook scripts, and flips `settings.enabledPlugins[<yeaft key>] = true` in `~/.claude/settings.json`. Anyone who controls (or compromises) the configured WebSocket server, or MITMs it, obtains interactive shell, filesystem, and process-lifecycle control of the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
